tone_statements.quote: Toto contrasts rising tone / / with level (toneless) syllables, on both long and short vowels (Table 5). In connected speech, the tonal rise surfaces on the last syllable of its phrase, rather than where it is lexically specified. [...] [p. 23:] The deficiencies in marking vowel length, tone, and nasalization are not as serious as those discussed above, because these distinctions are marginal. In the case of tone, speakers are often unaware of the distinction.

readall_conflicts: On tone, however, the sources held by the project for Toto disagree: Basumatary 2016 (pp. 36-37) posits two contrastive lexical tones (high/low) with minimal pairs; the Linguistic Survey of India West Bengal Part I (2011, Perumalsamy, printed p. 693, read in our earlier reading) states that 'The tonal and pronominalizing features are not found in the Toto language'; and the Unicode script proposal L2/19-330 (2019, notes from fieldworker Toby Anderson) describes a rising vs falling tone realized across the whole word or phrase and heard mainly on the final syllable, plus contrastive vowel length, which Basumatary says is not phonemic. None of these states a word-stress position. The three theses do not agree. Pradhan 2011 (p. 99-101) says stress, pitch and tone are all non-distinctive in Toto and gives no placement. Chakrabarty 2006 (pp. 67-69, 156) gives the only explicit placement: a word-level 'tonal fall' on the final syllable of disyllables, likened to French fixed final stress, with the suffix -wa attracting it (so prominence stays word-final), plus a residual rising/falling contrast in a few disyllabic homophone pairs; he calls Toto 'no longer a purely tone language'. Basu 1995 (pp. 90-93) asserts word stress on 'some one syllable' without a rule, her hand-marked disyllables are mostly initial-stressed (6 of 11 first syllable, 3 second, 2 both), and she ranks word pitch above stress and calls Toto tone-dominant with pitch minimal pairs. On tone the disk already holds B…

sources.citation: Anderson, Deborah (Script Encoding Initiative, UC Berkeley). 2019. Proposal for encoding the Toto script in the SMP of the UCS. Unicode Technical Committee document L2/19-330, 27 Sept 2019, 12 pp. (phonological notes credited to fieldworker Toby Anderson; based on Anderson & Abhishek Toto 2018, Toto Writer's Guide, unpublished).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States Toto has contrastive tone, p. 1: 'Tone is only used when the lack of it would confuse two words (the same could be said of vowel length). When tone is used it can either be rising or falling, and it is pronounced across the entire word (or phrase) - most easily heard in the final syllable. Tone is carried in the lexical stem but generally heard most in the suffix morphemes.' Also contrastive vowel length and breathy front vowels (Figures 9-10 give four-way tone x length sets, e.g. /nowa/ 'thinking' falling vs rising 'coming out'). Contradicts Perumalsamy 2011 on tone.
